passage:
A class group chat became messy. Students sent homework questions, jokes, stickers, arguments, and late-night messages in the same place.
Important announcements were missed.
The class created rules: homework questions before 9 p.m., no personal attacks, announcements pinned, and separate chats for games.
Some students thought rules would make the chat boring. Instead, it became more useful.
The group learned that digital spaces need structure just like classrooms. Without rules, the loudest or most frequent messages take over.
A chat group is not only a tool. It is a shared room made of words. Shared rooms need care.
